title: G20 Osaka Summit opens: Prime Minister Abe declares the start of "Osaka Truck" (June 28, 2019)
description: At the G20 Osaka Summit, which opened on the 28th, Prime Minister Abe, who will serve as chairman, announced that he will launch the "Osaka Truck," a framework to advance the creation of rules regarding the "digital economy."  ■Subscribe to the channel here https://yahoo.jp/zaoidV  ■THE PAGE - Make interesting news easy to understand https://yahoo.jp/g2tIKq  #thepage_jp #Press conference

asr.full_text: Thank you very much. ... We will now begin the Digital Economy Special Event. Thank you very much. Digitalization has changed the world of the economy and society rapidly. Through today's event, we hope that the momentum to promote international efforts related to the digital economy will be further strengthened. After this, I would like to thank Secretary of State Xi Jinping for his support. I also want to thank President Trump, Chairman of the European Council of the European Union, and the Director General of the Federal Office. Finally, I would like to conclude my speech. Thank you, President Xi. Second, we need to improve the rules of data management. Data is part of the digital economy, just like oil is part of the industrial economy. Effective data management requires both the collection, analysis, and application of data, and the self-management of the countries, ensuring the safety and usefulness of data. Thank you. Thank you. Next, we have a statement from the chairman of the European Union. Thank you. Thank you, Shinzo, for bringing us together. I will be very brief because we have other issues on our agenda. Electronic commerce has been tremendously growing over the last two decades. European Union strongly supports a predictable, effective, safe online environment for it. That is why we support Prime Minister Abe's data free flow with trust initiative. Electronic commerce does not stop at borders and so requires a global response. It is very encouraging to see so many countries involved. With 78 World Trade Organization members discussing 40 negotiating proposals, we have a very good basis to move forward and show that the organization can deliver in an ambitious way for the digital economy. I thank Prime Minister Abe for this Osaka trek. We should encourage our teams to make substantial progress in the negotiations by the Astana ministerial next year. Thanks. President Obama Thank you very much, Prime Minister Abe. It's an honor to join you and so many distinguished world leaders for this special session on the digital economy. American success on the digital economy. American success in the digital economy is based on free flow of data, strong privacy and intellectual property protection, access to capital, and innovation. The United States is committed to sustaining this approach to digital trade long into the future. We're eager to work with like-minded partners around the world to advance these priorities. The digital economy is a crucial driver of economic growth. At the same time as we expand digital trade, we must also ensure the resilience and security of our 5G networks. This is essential to our shared safety and prosperity. Further, the United States opposes data localization and policies which have been used to restrict digital trade flows and violate privacy and intellectual property protections. The United States seeks a future of digital trade that empowers all of our people. We look forward to working with other G20 members to advance an open, fair, and market-based digital economy that provides for the free flow of data and brings new prosperity to all of our nations. Thank you very much. Thank you very much. Next, we will have the Executive Director of WTO. barriers to entry affecting developing countries and smaller businesses the most, the 20th century showed that a fractured global trade order was not sustainable. That's why we created the multi-electrical system and the WTO. And the same is true today. We may well be working on a constitution for the economy of the 21st century. Prime Minister Abe has shown real leadership in placing global rules on the digital trade on the top of our priorities. The Osaka Trek commits the participants to promoting global rules on the digital trade. We are working to deliver this through the WTO, and we have already seen huge leaps forward being taken. Negotiations are now underway between 78 WTO members representing 90% of global trade. This is a real revolution in global trade. Most G20 members are on board. Determination exists, so we will see success. From this point of view, it is necessary to proceed with negotiations on the WTO's electronic trade. Currently, 78 countries and regions are involved in the WTO's electronic tradeling Conference is still a great opportunity to achieve results. Also, we need to pay tribute to the challenges facing other countries, like the LTC. We will keep working on it. Thank you all for your cooperation. Thank you very much. I'd like to ask the press corps to leave the room first. I'm not very good, but I know that I can win. He's my buddy, I'm always happy to see him. Who's your friend? Me! Me too!

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it depicts news coverage of a formal G20 digital-economy event, with officials discussing data management, electronic commerce and international digital-trade rules. The request to subscribe is ordinary audience engagement and is not presented as a condition for receiving money, investing, providing credentials or joining a financial scheme. The end screen identifies the publisher's latest news videos.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary context is general news coverage of an international summit, including officials' prepared remarks and a news-publisher end screen, rather than a scam mechanism or a financial participation offer.
